statements.quote: The user interface for the study was implemented using React while any data collection and the interaction with the OpenAI API for GPT-4o was performed by a NodeJS server. All processing of the prompts, randomization of tasks, etc. was performed on the server to ensure the integrity of the data.
statements.locator: p. 6, Section 3.4 (Apparatus), first paragraph; implementation/data-handling description, not a code-release statement.

statements.quote: While participants created memes, we recorded all ideas they came up with, both text and images, as well as a full log of their interaction with the LLM and its responses on the server. For recording the subjective perception, we used a commercial survey platform. The survey included questions for the participants to self-assess their creativity, as well as the NASA-TLX and general questions about the interface and the ideation process. We used the same platform for rating the generated ideas as well. Demographic data was provided via Prolific, which we used for participant recruiting.
statements.locator: p. 6, Section 3.5 (Data Collection), complete paragraph; describes the collected data, without promising public access.

notes: Checked 2026-10-09. Read all 61,327 characters of the saved markdown, including the references and end of the document; there are no appendices in the 11-page saved article. Checked the two supplementary-material statements against PDF pp. 5-6 and inspected PDF link annotations and embedded-file metadata (no embedded files). The saved source is the author's arXiv version; the publisher's Version of Record was not inspected. The paper promises supplementary prompts and fully AI-generated captions, not release of participant-level data, participant captions, ratings, or analysis code. The implementation and data-collection quotations describe what was built/recorded and are not availability promises. No preregistration link, data/code repository link, license for a dataset, or on-request data statement was found. Both data_and_code URL fields in forms/c168.json are empty. The article DOI https://doi.org/10.1145/3708359.3712094 redirected to https://dl.acm.org/doi/10.1145/3708359.3712094 and returned HTTP 403 with a Cloudflare 'Just a moment...' bot-check page. Stopped at that check; the existence, filenames, contents, and access terms of publisher-hosted supplements remain unverified. This is not evidence that a data deposit requires an account or author approval. As an independent source, https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.11433 returned HTTP 200 and exposed a source-archive link but no dedicated supplementary/data link. https://arxiv.org/src/2501.11433 returned HTTP 200 (application/gzip; 1,574,399 bytes), downloaded and inspected entirely in memory. Its 20 regular files were ACM LaTeX/style/bibliography/build files and article figures: acmart.cls, acmauthoryear.bbx, acmauthoryear.cbx, acmdatamodel.dbx, acmnumeric.bbx, acmnumeric.cbx, ACM-Reference-Format.bst, comment.cut, main.bbl, main.out, main.tex, sample-base.bib, images/meme-rating-all-topics.pdf, images/number-of-ideas.pdf, images/phase1.jpg, images/phase2.jpg, images/task.jpg, images/teaser.jpg, images/tlx.pdf, and images/UI.jpg. No participant table, rating table, full caption list, study-interface code, or analysis code was present. main.tex repeated the two supplementary-material statements without a repository URL. This article/source archive is excluded from deposits because it is a manuscript package, not a data/code/study-material deposit. Bibliographic links to other papers are not c168 deposits. No relevant repository identifier was found for a file-list API request. The searches did not establish that data are unavailable everywhere; in particular, the blocked publisher supplement and the OSF title-filter limitation prevent high confidence. Without confirmed participant IDs, condition labels and outcomes/texts, none of final.open_items can be resolved from public data: arm/test counts, rating aggregation and scale, idea-count analysis rows, participant-level means/SDs/SEs or pairwise effect sizes, and the distinct creators of the sampled memes remain unknown. Diversity measures cannot be computed from a confirmed public participant-caption corpus, and allocation randomization remains unverified.
